Structure and Functions of Citizen Participation Groups
The citizen participation structure of the CDBG Program provides for citizens to address community development needs and make recommendations at three levels: (1) through a central Community Development Steering Committee, (2) at Planning Area Committee meetings held in the Alum Rock, Central and Alviso Planning Areas, and (3) at City Council public hearings. The structure consists of two types of citizen committees as follows:
1. Community Development Block Grant Steering Committee 
(a) Membership (refer to Project Description)
(b) Functions
The Community Development Block Grant Steering Committee is proposed to remain as the lead citizen participation group in the planning, programming process of the Community Development Block Grant. As shown on the attached schedule, the Steering Committee should be involved in the total CDBG planning process. Their specific responsibilities should be:
(1) To advise the City Administration and the City Council in the selection of activity areas and the development of the Community Development Plan and Program.
(2) To conduct public meetings on the development of the program and the selection of activity areas and to review and evaluate proposals from community groups.
(3) To assist the City Council in conducting public hearings on the program.
2. Community Development Activity Area Committees 
(a) Memberships
These committees are composed of residents of the specific planning areas as delineated by the City Council.
(b) Functions
These committees report directly to the Steering Committee. They provide the Steering Committee with information and recommendations on:
(1) Target area needs
(2) Program proposals
(3) Plan document
Citizen Involvement in the Planning Process
1. Submissions of Views
Citizens will be given many opportunities during the planning process to submit views and proposals. Proposals and views will also be presented at scheduled area meetings and before the City Council at any of three public hearings.
